propositions: Pandoc invocations can hang indefinitely on pathological input (observed 13.5 min at 95.8% CPU) because pypandoc provides no timeout and subprocess.run(timeout=) reaps only direct child, not grandchild pipe holders.
Current subprocess.run(timeout=30) in _convert does not kill spawned process groups, allowing CPU-spinning grandchildren to survive after timeout expiration.
Pandoc GPL license and binary provenance (via pypandoc-binary wheel) must be recorded and verified to comply with licensing obligations.

Process-group reaping via start_new_session=True and rebar._proc.reap_process_group, with caller-side communicate(input=markdown, timeout=) will eliminate hung processes while preserving per-unit fallback semantics.
Configuration key reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s (default 10s) must be exposed across config schema, environment, and documentation to make timeout tunable.
